archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (bullpen-and-glove)
archetype.definition: A 91-win wild card that swept its opening series, then lost three of four one-run-or-close games to Milwaukee because a league-average lineup couldn't score behind a staff that kept it in every game.

report.headline: A 91-win record built on Mason Miller, elite gloves and close-game luck

recap.finish: 91-71, second in the NL West; swept CHC 2-0 in the Wild Card Series, lost the NLDS 1-3 to MIL
recap.body:
This was a run-prevention team in a pitcher's park (94). The lineup was ordinary: 16th in runs per game and 18th in OPS at .717. The defense was third in Fielding Runs, and one of the league's best late-inning bullpens finished games. The record ran ahead of the team. San Diego outscored opponents by 41 runs over 162 games (+0.25 per game, 10th), a margin that usually produces about 85 wins. The other six came from a +5.7 W vs Run Diff, third-highest in the league.

The season came in three acts. After a 1-4 March, an 18-7 April on a +21 run margin made the Padres look like a real threat to the Dodgers. Then May through July went 37-43 while they were outscored by 22 runs, and the team was a .500 club in every sense. August and September (17-11, then 18-6) went 35-17 with a +55 margin, closing on an 8-2 run that included two of three at Dodger Stadium. Even so, they finished nine games behind a 100-win Los Angeles and entered October as a wild card.

Three players carried the offense. Fernando Tatis Jr. produced 5.4 WAR with a 131 wRC+ and 38 steals. Ty France had a 141 wRC+ in 500 PA, the best rate on the club. Jackson Merrill added 4.2 WAR with 26 homers and 27 steals. Around them the lineup thinned. Manny Machado hit 30 homers but only .217/.303, a 98 wRC+. Bogaerts (95), Cronenworth (83), Rengifo (82) and catcher Freddy Fermin (68) gave back much of what the top produced. The hitters still graded a B, which suggests the league's lineups were not much deeper.

The pitching was split between the two groups. Mason Miller was the No. 1 reliever on the site out of 389: 1.67 ERA, 1.17 FIP, 47.4% strikeouts and 38 saves. Adrian Morejon (5th) and Bradgley Rodriguez (18th) made the bridge to him nearly as strong. The rotation graded a D, and its ERAs flattered it. Michael King's 3.21 came with a 4.13 FIP. Robbie Ray's 3.59 came with a 4.69 FIP and a 12% walk rate. No starter struck out more than 21% of hitters. The defense and the park absorbed a lot of contact that a lesser setup would have turned into runs.

October followed the same script. The Padres shut down Chicago 8-0 and 4-1, allowing one run in two games. Against Milwaukee they lost 3-2 and 4-3 on the road, won 4-3 at home, and lost 3-1. That is ten runs in four games, with all three losses by a combined four runs. The staff posted a 2.22 postseason ERA (3rd of 12), and King allowed one earned run in 14 innings. The lineup managed a .651 OPS, Tatis hit .167, and the close-game edge from the summer flipped to -1.2. Machado's 200 wRC+ in 25 PA was the best thing the bats did, and every postseason line here is a handful of plate appearances.

In context, this was a fifth straight winning season, and the third-best record of the five. It was not one of the stronger teams of the run. The run margin was the lowest since 2022. The 3.99 ERA was the worst since 2021. Run prevention slipped from 2nd to 9th even as Fielding Runs jumped from -1.5 to 28.6, by far the best mark of the stretch.

highlights.title: Mason Miller and the late innings
highlights.body: Miller was the best reliever on the site by a wide margin, striking out nearly half the hitters he faced, with a FIP even lower than his ERA. Morejon (2.37 FIP, 28 holds) and Rodriguez (2.19 ERA) gave the Padres a three-man late-inning group that let them win close games. That group is a large part of why the W vs Run Diff ran so high. The skill underneath (strikeouts, a low FIP) is real and should hold. The one-run record it produced will not repeat as reliably.

highlights.title: A defense that saved the rotation
highlights.body: The Padres were third in Fielding Runs, with Machado, France, Merrill, Tatis and Fermin all at +5 or better. Coming off a slightly below-average 2025, that defense is what turned a low-strikeout rotation with FIPs mostly in the 4s into a 3.99 team ERA. Fielding numbers swing more year to year than hitting or pitching, so expect some give-back.

highlights.title: Tatis, France and Merrill
highlights.body: Three hitters produced 13.2 WAR between them. Tatis combined on-base ability, power and 38 steals. France was the most productive hitter per plate appearance. Merrill added 26 homers and 27 steals with plus defense in center. The B grade for the hitters rests largely on these three.

lowlights.title: A rotation the ERAs overstate
lowlights.body: The starters graded a D, and their ERAs read better than the work underneath. Ray's FIP was more than a run above his ERA, he walked 12% of hitters, and King's FIP was 4.13. With Vásquez striking out under 15%, the group leaned on its defense and a pitcher-friendly park. If either of those supports weakens, this rotation's run totals rise.

lowlights.title: The bottom of the order
lowlights.body: Outside the top three, the lineup ran below average. Machado's 30 homers came with a .217 average, and four regulars, Fermin at catcher among them, finished at 83 wRC+ or worse. That is how a team with three strong hitters ends up 16th in runs. It is also why ten runs in four NLDS games was not a surprise.

lowlights.title: Wins the margin didn't earn
lowlights.body: A +0.25 run differential per game projects to roughly 85 wins, not 91. The 5.7-win gap was the league's third-largest. Some of that is the bullpen, but most close-game edges even out, and this one reversed in October.

arc.note: A hot April (18-7) gave way to three months of losing ball and a negative run margin. Then a 35-17 finish over August and September carried them into the wild card, though still nine games behind the Dodgers.

recap.nextYear: The core that carries forward is clear: Tatis, Merrill and France at the plate, and Miller, Morejon and Rodriguez at the end of games. Those are skill-backed performances, not flukes. Several things that propped up the record are less durable. Six wins came from close-game outcomes beyond the run margin. A defense that jumped to third in Fielding Runs from below average a year earlier is due to give some back. And a rotation's ERAs sat well under its FIPs. If those normalize, this is closer to an 85-win team with a D-graded rotation. The two groups that most need work are the starting staff, which lacks strikeouts behind King, and the second half of the lineup, including catcher and second base. Griffin Canning pitching the most bullpen innings with a 5.68 ERA is also a gap behind the top three relievers. The year-over-year trend is a warning: run differential and team ERA both slipped from 2024-25, even as the record held steady.

confidence.note: Full 162-game season; postseason lines are tiny samples of 25 PA or fewer per hitter.
